P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Restricted in practice. TRAP: the Bank of Papua New Guinea requires all funds held in PNG to be held in kina (PGK), so foreign receipts end up in kina. Foreign-exchange shortages can make conversion and transfers abroad slow or impossible (trade.gov).

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: The TIN (Taxpayer Identification Number), issued by the Internal Revenue Commission (IRC). Small businesses register on the IRC's Small Business Tax TIN registration form (IRC TIN4I, under the Income Tax Act 1959, effective 21 May 2021), which asks for identity, business location and estimated turnover (IRC). Local banks reportedly will not open an account without a TIN (search summary).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed). The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
